To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alfalfa silages ensiled with or without SO2 have similar digestibility by lactating dairy cows.
the alfalfa silages had different chemical compositions, but similar monosaccharides were digested in the rumen of dairy cows fed diets containing these silages.
the digestibilities of glucose and total carbohydrate were similar in TMR containing alfalfa silage made from either fresh alfalfa alone or from a mixture of 30% wheat treated with SO2 and 70% fresh.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of alfalfa silage type on the digestibility by dairy cattle of the monosaccharides in alfalfa silage and in the TMR.
the effect of alfalfa silage on the digestibility by dairy cattle of glucose, xylose and other constituents of neutral detergent-sugar fractions of alfalfa.
the effects of alfalfa silage on the digestibility by dairy cattle of the monosaccharides in the diet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alfalfa silage can replace alfalfa hay in TMR for dairy cows and that the digestibility of the monosaccharides in alfalfa silage is similar to that in alfalfa hay.
the alfalfa silages did not influence monosaccharides in TMR digestibility.
alfalfa silage and the silage of 30% alfalfa + 70% wheat straw treated in the same manner had a similar effect on digestibility of DM and OM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the digestibility of neutral detergent-sugar constituents of alfalfa silage was similar to that of the alfalfa silage of alfalfawheat straw treated with SO 2.

digestibilities of glucose, xylose and total carbohydrates in TMR were similar for cows fed silage of alfafa or alfalfa plus wheat treated with SO2, but that the digestibility of NDF xylose in alfalfa silage was greater than in alfalfa plus wheat silage.
the digestibility of neutral detergent-sugars was high, but the digestibility of non-neutral detergent-sugars and neutral detergent-sugarcos was low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alfalfa silages can be fed to dairy cows in place of alfalfa hay with no adverse effect on the digestibility by cows of monosacharides of the TMR.
dairy cows can utilize monosaccharides from forages and concentrates in TMRs.
the digestibility of the monosaccharides in alfalfa silage was similar when alfalfa was ensiled with or without the addition of wheat straw treated with sulfur dioxide.
